dialogues.speaker: Navaratra
dialogues.text: Natlan's gemstones are unique. They appear very lively, but they tend to be quite rough.

dialogues.speaker: Philpot
dialogues.text: It's a matter of craftsmanship. Natlanese gemstone cutting isn't as sophisticated as it is in Fontaine and Sumeru. There aren't many fine details you can examine.

dialogues.speaker: Navaratra
dialogues.text: No, it's got nothing to do with craftsmanship. In a tribe called the Children of Echoes, I once saw Honey Pearls worked with breathtaking skill. They've just never really made a splash on the international market.

dialogues.speaker: Philpot
dialogues.text: And why do you think that is?

dialogues.speaker: Navaratra
dialogues.text: The way I see it, it's a matter of choice. Natlan has no shortage of skilled craftsmen, but they choose to sell products that are simple.

dialogues.speaker: Navaratra
dialogues.text: Perhaps they prefer raw, unfiltered wildness — your Fontainian notions of intricacy and delicate patterns hold no sway here.

dialogues.speaker: Navaratra
dialogues.text: Complexity adds depth, yet raises barriers. Simplicity lacks grandeur, but flows unbound. If you wish to thrive here with your jewelry trade, ignore this at your peril.

dialogues.speaker: Philpot
dialogues.text: Hmm... You make an interesting point. I shall take note.
